title.narrative: Multi-sectoral Emergency Response to Conflict-Affected Communities in Eastern Zone of Tigray Region, Ethiopia

description.narrative:
ltpgtlt/pgtltpgtEthiopia has been continued in facing different humanitarian challenges that majorly caused by conflict, drought and seasonal floods. Ethiopia is the third largest refugee hosting country in Africa, home to more than 930,000 refugees and asylum seekers—mainly from South Sudan, Somalia, and Eritrea. The primary shocks that have led to protracted displacement in Ethiopia are related to ethnic and/or territorial conflict and drought. According to Ethiopia’s 2023 HRP, there were an estimated 4.6 million IDPs in the country. Even though the 2023 Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP) targets over 20 million people at a cost of $3.99 billion the current portion reached very minimal. lt/pgt
ltpgtAs known, conflict broke out between the Ethiopian government and a regional defense force, the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) armed (November 2020). As a result, thousands killed and millions internally displaced. After two years of conflict, a peace deal was signed in November 2022 that created good platform for better humanitarian access. In the Tigray region, responding to the emergency needs of affected populations, mainly as a consequence of the two-year conflict in northern Ethiopia, remains a priority. Recent site assessments and a village assessment survey identified more than 1 million people displaced in 643 sites across six zones (excluding 20 woredas/ districts hard to reach due to security or environmental factors), and 1.26 million returning IDPs (internally displaced persons) in 963 villages across five zones in the region (IOM site assessment round 33, June 2023).lt/pgt
ltpgtAdigrat town is located in the Easter zone having more than 10 thousand IDPs among 647HH (3235 individuals) hosted in five collective centers and they are in need of critical humanitarian assistance. Among these IDPs’, currently about 460 HHs are settled in three schools that should be urgently under need for teaching and learning resume. As the current quick need verification need assessment revealed the three schools (Finotebirhane 2”, Agazi 1” and Meda-Agame 1”) those hosting the IDPs still, learning school for more than three thousand students.lt/pgt
ltpgtThe preliminary needs that are identified by partners on 3 August are shelter and non-food items (ESNFI), food, protection, as well as, health and water, sanitation, and hygiene services (WASH). Indeed, there are more than 5,157 students are out of school due to the schools occupied by the IDPs’ in Adigrat town and scholastic materials, school feeding and maintenance of rooms among priority needs as per ZOA/ASDEP quick assessment.lt/pgt
ltpgtThe proposed intervention will support the IDPs’ move/transfer from the school in Adigrat by assisting the IDPs who are moved/transferred from the schools to alternate sites alternative shelter options and resumption of activities in the school through basic repairs and site decommissioning following IDPs departure from the collective sites. As suggested for EHF 1st allocation and based on the priority needs identified by ZOA, ASDEPO and other actors the action focuses on WASH, S/NFI, Education and protection considering the CVA modality.lt/pgt
